outcome: Persistent delay in visual-spatial cognitive tests
cohort: 8845 participants from the Millennium Cohort Study, a nationally representative UK cohort
finding: Planned cesarean section was associated with a small increase in the risk of visual-spatial cognitive delay in childhood.
mod_finding: Planned cesarean section was associated with a statistically significant association with visual-spatial cognitive delay at age 5 and 7, as well as increased odds of 'early childhood delay' and borderline increased odds of 'persistent delay' in visual-spatial cognitive tests.
